stories.headline: TSMC CEO warns chip supply won't meet AI-fueled demand for years

key_facts.fact: TSMC CEO C.C. Wei told shareholders on June 4 that the company's global chip supply will fall short of AI-fueled demand for years to come, even as more US capacity comes online.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC won't be able to fulfill demand led by American customers even as more manufacturing capacity comes online in the US over the next few years, Wei told shareholders on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: Wei said TSMC will refrain from the kind of abrupt price hikes that shook up the memory sector, prioritizing stable business over margin expansion.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC will refrain from the sort of abrupt price hikes that shook up the memory chip sector, Wei added. TSMC's intent is to ensure a stable business.

key_facts.fact: Wei reiterated TSMC's forecast for sales growth of more than 30% in 2026, with capex trending toward the upper end of a $56 billion range.
key_facts.excerpt: He reiterated its forecast for sales growth of more than 30 per cent for this year... its own capital spending should trend towards the upper end of an existing forecast range of as much as US$56 billion.

key_facts.fact: Wei said hyperscalers are set to spend $725 billion on AI this year, far outstripping TSMC's expansion plans.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC has been expanding its footprint beyond its home island to add capacity, yet even that is not enough to satisfy chip needs as major hyperscalers are set to spend US$725 billion for AI just this year.

key_facts.fact: Asked whether TSMC could raise prices, Wei said he would 'like to do that' but would never push toward 80% gross margins like some memory peers.
key_facts.excerpt: Asked during the shareholder meeting whether TSMC could raise prices for customers, Wei said he would 'like to do that'... 'I envy 80% gross margins, but I would never do that,' Wei told reporters.

stories.headline: Broadcom Q2 sales grow 48% to $22.2B but AI guidance underwhelms; shares fall 12%+

key_facts.fact: Broadcom reported Q2 fiscal 2026 revenue of $22.19 billion, up 48% YoY, missing analyst estimates of $22.27 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Second-quarter revenue of $22.19 billion missed estimates of $22.27 billion, as Broadcom races with Nvidia whose dominant graphics processing units remain the industry standard for AI workloads.

key_facts.fact: Q2 AI semiconductor revenue reached $10.8 billion, up 143% YoY, driven by demand for custom AI accelerators and AI networking.
key_facts.excerpt: Q2 semiconductor revenue from AI of $10.8 billion grew 143% year-over-year, above our forecast, driven by increasing demand for custom AI accelerators and AI networking.

key_facts.fact: Broadcom forecast Q3 AI chip revenue of $16 billion, slightly below analyst estimates of $16.36 billion, and stuck to a long-range forecast of $100 billion in AI chip sales.
key_facts.excerpt: Broadcom also said it expects AI chip revenue of $16 billion in its current third quarter, slightly below estimates of $16.36 billion... CEO Hock Tan said the company is keeping its AI semiconductor revenue guidance for its fiscal 2027 at 'in excess of $100 billion.'

key_facts.fact: CEO Hock Tan said Broadcom now expects to ship more than 10 gigawatts of AI chip compute in 2027 and 'a lot more' in 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: Hock Tan said Broadcom now expects to ship more than 10 gigawatts' worth of AI chips in 2027 - a slight increase from previous estimates - but stuck to the company's long-range forecast of $100 billion in sales from those chips.

key_facts.fact: AVGO shares fell more than 12% in pre-market trading on June 4, dragging Micron and SanDisk down more than 6%.
key_facts.excerpt: The stock off more than 12% in premarket trading... Micron and Sandisk are both down more than 6% on Thursday, as Broadcom's underwhelming results weigh on the entire AI complex.

key_facts.fact: Broadcom guided Q3 revenue of approximately $29.4 billion, an 84% YoY increase, above analyst estimate of $28.54 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Third quarter fiscal year 2026 revenue guidance of approximately $29.4 billion, an increase of 84 percent from the prior year period.

stories.headline: Robotics startup Generalist AI raises $400M at $2B valuation led by Radical Ventures

key_facts.fact: Generalist AI, a robotics startup, raised $400 million in a new funding round at a $2 billion valuation, announced Thursday June 4.
key_facts.excerpt: Generalist AI, a robotics startup, has raised $400 million in a new funding round to develop more sophisticated artificial intelligence models meant to help robots handle increasingly complex tasks... The financing, set to be announced on Thursday, values Generalist at $2 billion, including the money raised.

key_facts.fact: Radical Ventures led the round with participation from 8VC, Union Square Ventures, Hanabi Capital, plus existing investors Nvidia and Bezos Expeditions.
key_facts.excerpt: Radical Ventures led the round with participation from venture firms 8VC, Union Square Ventures and Hanabi Capital, as well as existing investors Nvidia Corp. and Bezos Expeditions.

key_facts.fact: Generalist AI was founded by Pete Florence, Andy Zeng, and Andy Barry, and is known for training large-parameter models from scratch.
key_facts.excerpt: Generalist AI, founded by Pete Florence, Andy Zeng, and Andy Barry, is part of a growing crop of startups applying AI advances to the field of robotics.

key_facts.fact: Generalist released its GEN-1 model for short physical tasks in April and recently joined Nvidia's Cosmos Coalition for open world models.
key_facts.excerpt: Generalist AI: Known for its strict conviction in training large parameter counts entirely from scratch, Generalist AI has joined the coalition... continuing the push for 'intelligent improvisation' seen in their recent GEN-1 model rollout.

stories.headline: Quantinuum raises $1.68B in upsized IPO at $15.6B valuation, sets new bar for quantum

key_facts.fact: Honeywell-backed Quantinuum priced its upsized US IPO at $60 per share on June 3, selling 28 million shares to raise $1.68 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Quantinuum today announced the pricing of the upsized initial public offering of 28,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock at a price to the public of $60.00 per share.

key_facts.fact: The pricing was above the marketed range of $53 to $55, valuing Quantinuum at $15.6 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The offering, which was upsized from 26.5 million shares, priced above its marketed range of $53 to $55, and values the company at $15.6 billion, based on the outstanding shares in its filings.

key_facts.fact: The offering was upsized from a planned 26.5 million shares, with underwriters granted a 30-day option for up to 4.2 million additional shares.
key_facts.excerpt: Quantinuum has granted the underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 4,200,000 shares of its Class A common stock to cover over-allotments.

key_facts.fact: Shares begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Market on June 4 under the ticker QNT, with JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, Jefferies, and Evercore leading the offering.
key_facts.excerpt: The shares of Class A common stock are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Market on June 4, 2026 under the ticker symbol 'QNT.'

key_facts.fact: Quantinuum was formed in 2021 by merging Honeywell's quantum business with Cambridge Quantum and is targeting a fault-tolerant machine called Apollo for 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: It was formed in 2021 from the merger of Honeywell's quantum business and Cambridge Quantum, and it builds quantum computers aimed at problems classical machines would take impractically long to solve. The company is working towards a fault-tolerant machine it calls Apollo, targeted for 2029.

stories.headline: Foxconn and Intel announce strategic partnership on next-gen AI infrastructure

key_facts.fact: Foxconn and Intel announced on June 4 a strategic collaboration to jointly develop AI infrastructure spanning silicon, racks, systems, and applications.
key_facts.excerpt: Foxconn on Thursday announced a strategic partnership with Intel to develop end-to-end AI solutions. The companies said they will jointly explore AI offerings spanning chips, racks, systems, and applications.

key_facts.fact: The partnership will build rack-scale AI infrastructure systems combining Intel Xeon processors with AI accelerators, plus high-speed interconnects, liquid cooling, and scalable data center architectures.
key_facts.excerpt: In AI infrastructure, Foxconn and Intel will work on rack-scale systems built around Intel Xeon processors and AI accelerators. The partnership will also focus on high-speed interconnects, thermal management, liquid cooling, system monitoring, and scalable AI data center architectures.

key_facts.fact: Beyond infrastructure, the companies will also collaborate on custom ASIC design and system integration services.
key_facts.excerpt: Beyond infrastructure, Foxconn said it will explore opportunities with Intel in custom ASIC design and system integration services.

key_facts.fact: At Computex on June 2, Intel had already pre-announced racks combining Xeon processors with SambaNova SN-50 RDUs, with Foxconn providing systems integration.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel, SambaNova, and Foxconn today announced their intent to build rackscale AI infrastructure for data center, hyperscale, and intelligence center deployments—built on Intel Xeon processors... As part of the collaboration, Foxconn will provide system integration capabilities for the new rackscale AI infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: A single liquid-cooled Xeon 6+ rack can deliver 36,864 cores in 32U at roughly 100 kW of rack power.
key_facts.excerpt: A single liquid-cooled rack can deliver 36,864 cores using 32U of compute space, which provides the highest agent density available (at approximately 100-kilowatt rack power compute).

stories.headline: Grimes County approves 35-year tax abatement for SpaceX's $55B Terafab chip plant

key_facts.fact: Grimes County commissioners voted 4-1 on June 3 to approve a reinvestment zone and 100% property tax abatement for SpaceX's Terafab semiconductor facility.
key_facts.excerpt: On Wednesday, Grimes County commissioners voted 4-1 to approve both a reinvestment zone designation and a 100% tax abatement for SpaceX's proposed Terafab semiconductor chip manufacturing facility.

key_facts.fact: The tax abatement lasts 35 years and is initially valued at $55 billion, with potential to scale to $119 billion across multiple phases.
key_facts.excerpt: Grimes County, Texas, just handed SpaceX a full property tax waiver lasting 35 years for a planned $55B semiconductor manufacturing facility called Terafab... a project initially valued at $55 billion with the potential to scale to $119 billion across multiple phases.

key_facts.fact: Under the PILOT (payments in lieu of taxes) structure, SpaceX will pay $10M upfront and $20M annually, totaling about $710M over 35 years.
key_facts.excerpt: In exchange for the 100% property tax abatement, SpaceX will pay an upfront fee of $10M and annual payments of $20M over the 35-year term. Quick math: that's $710M in total payments to the county.

key_facts.fact: The project, planned for the former Gibbons Creek Power Plant site, would aim to provide 'a terawatt of computing power each year,' more than 10 times the current capacity of all AI infrastructure, per SpaceX.
key_facts.excerpt: The plant project's ultimate goal is to provide a terawatt of computing power each year to the technology giants, more than 10 times the current capacity of all AI infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: More than 100 residents attended a heated hearing warning the project could strain water and power, harm wildlife, and alter the county's rural character.
key_facts.excerpt: The vote came after a heated hearing that drew more than 100 residents to the Grimes County courthouse. Speakers warned the project could strain water and power supplies, harm wildlife and permanently alter the county's rural character.

stories.headline: Amazon unveils next-gen Proteus warehouse robot that takes plain-language commands

key_facts.fact: Amazon unveiled a next-generation Proteus warehouse robot at its 'Delivering the Future' event in Dartford, near London, on June 4.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon unveiled a next-generation Proteus robot and more ultra-fast delivery options, plus a European fulfillment workforce expansion.

key_facts.fact: The new Proteus can operate anywhere across fulfillment sites and accepts text-based conversational prompts, without technical commands or programming interfaces.
key_facts.excerpt: The next generation of Amazon's autonomous Proteus robot can now operate anywhere items need to be moved across sites—not just in dock areas. Using advances in AI, employees can now direct Proteus with plain, conversational text-based prompts.

key_facts.fact: Proteus can move heavy carts weighing up to about 400 kg (882 lbs) and is currently in lab pilots; European deployment is planned for the first half of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The current version can transport carts weighing nearly 400 kilograms, or about 882 pounds. The next-generation model is expected to arrive at European sites in the first half of 2027.

key_facts.fact: Amazon also announced more than €10 billion (~$11.6B) of investment in European fulfillment over the coming years, plus 25,000 new jobs.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon is investing more than €10 billion over the coming years to expand and modernize fulfillment centers across Europe... Amazon plans to grow its European fulfillment center workforce by 25,000.

key_facts.fact: The current Proteus is already operating at 25 Amazon facilities across the United States, primarily moving heavy carts in dock areas.
key_facts.excerpt: Proteus is already operating at 25 Amazon facilities across the United States, where it primarily moves heavy carts in dock areas.

key_facts.fact: Amazon also expanded STARK, a collaborative tote-handling robot, planning rollout to 15 European sites by 2027, plus Vulcan, a robot with a 'sense of touch,' now in Hamburg.
key_facts.excerpt: STARK, a collaborative tote-handling robot first piloted in Barcelona and set to reach 15 European sites by 2027, and Vulcan, the company's first robot with a sense of touch, which has moved from Spokane, Washington to its Hamburg facility.
